comparisons.peer_topic: Composition and credit quality of debt securities portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, the Corporation held predominantly U.S. agency and Treasury securities with a zero credit loss assumption, alongside significant holdings in FNMA and FHLMC securities. The portfolio included non-U.S. securities for regulatory compliance, and nonperforming AFS debt securities were not significant.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan (MS) and Bank of America (BAC) disclose that the vast majority of their Held-to-Maturity (HTM) and debt securities portfolios consist of high-quality U.S. agency and Treasury securities, for which they apply a zero credit loss assumption. MS states that 98% of its HTM portfolio comprises these securities with an assumption of zero credit losses. Similarly, BAC reports that $871.1 billion (out of a total of ~$908.6 billion AFS+HTM) consisted predominantly of U.S. agency and Treasury securities with a zero credit loss assumption. Both firms treat the non-investment grade or remaining portion of the portfolio as having insignificant expected credit losses.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, 98% of the Firm's portfolio of HTM securities were investment grade U.S. agency securities, U.S. Treasury securities and Agency CMBS, which were on accrual status and for which there is an underlying assumption of zero credit losses.

Non-investment grade HTM securities primarily consisted of certain Non-agency CMBS securities, for which the expected credit losses were insignificant and were predominantly on accrual status at December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023.
At December 31, 2024 and 2023, $871.1 billion and $824.9 billion of AFS and HTM debt securities, which were predominantly U.S. agency and U.S. Treasury securities, have a zero credit loss assumption.
For the same periods, the ECL on the remaining $37.5 billion and $40.2 billion of AFS and HTM debt securities were insignificant.

comparisons.peer_topic: Status of HTM debt securities regarding delinquency and non-accrual status
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi reported no held-to-maturity (HTM) debt securities that were delinquent or on non-accrual status as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and Citi provide assurance regarding the credit quality and status of their HTM debt securities. MS notes that its investment grade HTM securities were on accrual status with an assumption of zero credit losses, and non-investment grade holdings had insignificant expected credit losses. Citi explicitly states it had no HTM debt securities that were delinquent or on non-accrual status, supporting the same conclusion of strong credit quality and lack of impairment in the HTM portfolio.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, 98% of the Firm's portfolio of HTM securities were investment grade U.S. agency securities, U.S. Treasury securities and Agency CMBS, which were on accrual status and for which there is an underlying assumption of zero credit losses.

Non-investment grade HTM securities primarily consisted of certain Non-agency CMBS securities, for which the expected credit losses were insignificant and were predominantly on accrual status at December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023.
Citi did not have any HTM debt securities that were delinquent or on non-accrual status at December 31, 2024 and 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair Value Measurement Assumptions for Mortgage-Backed Retained Interests
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm uses weighted average key economic assumptions to measure the fair value of mortgage-backed retained interests, where discount rates for non-agency interests include expected credit losses and sensitivity analysis indicates that adverse assumption changes are not linear or independent.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS discuss the treatment of credit losses in the context of U.S. government agency securities. MS explicitly states that its U.S. agency securities are held with an underlying assumption of zero credit losses. GS discloses that for mortgage-backed retained interests related to U.S. government agency-issued CMOs, the discount rate does not include any credit loss, consistent with the low credit risk profile of agency paper. Both disclosures highlight the distinction between agency securities (zero/no credit loss assumption) and non-agency/non-U.S. securities (which do include credit loss assumptions).

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, 98% of the Firm's portfolio of HTM securities were investment grade U.S. agency securities, U.S. Treasury securities and Agency CMBS, which were on accrual status and for which there is an underlying assumption of zero credit losses.

• The discount rate for retained interests that relate to U.S. government agency-issued CMOs does not include any credit loss. Expected credit loss assumptions are reflected in the discount rate for the remainder of retained interests.

comparisons.peer_topic: HTM securities credit quality and ratings
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, all Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities were rated investment grade, current, and accruing, with approximately 99% rated at least AA+ based on external or internal risk ratings.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPMorgan disclose that their Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities portfolios are composed entirely or nearly entirely of investment grade securities. MS states that 98% of its HTM portfolio consisted of investment grade U.S. agency, Treasury, and Agency CMBS securities. JPMorgan reports that all its HTM securities were rated investment grade, with approximately 99% rated at least AA+. Both disclosures emphasize the high credit quality of the HTM holdings.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, 98% of the Firm's portfolio of HTM securities were investment grade U.S. agency securities, U.S. Treasury securities and Agency CMBS, which were on accrual status and for which there is an underlying assumption of zero credit losses.

At both December 31, 2024 and 2023, all HTM securities were rated investment grade and were current and accruing, with approximately 99% rated at least AA+ (based upon external ratings where available, and where not available, based primarily upon internal risk ratings).
